name: Grok Bot

surfaces.label: Grok Bot desktop app (Electron 42.1.0, internal name "sand"). A CLIENT of Bots that run on a Cursor-hosted cloud computer, not the agent itself: closing the app does not stop a turn. The main process argv[0] is the full path of Contents/MacOS/Grok Bot (CFBundleExecutable `Grok Bot`, bundle id com.anysphere.sand, both read from the 0.63.0 Info.plist). Electron helpers (Grok Bot Helper, Grok Bot Helper (Renderer), (GPU), (Plugin)) live under Contents/Frameworks and do not match; neither does the macOS computer-use helper Contents/Helpers/Grok Bot Computer Use.app (executable CUGrokBotService, bundle co.anysphere.grok-bot-computer-use). Not the Grok Build CLI (`grok-build` row).

local-exec daemon: the process that runs commands the cloud Bot sends to THIS Mac, only when Execution on Local Computer is Ask every time (the default) or Always allow. CORRECTED from the 0.18.0 teardown. In 0.63.0 the main process forks it as an Electron utility process (utilityProcess.fork of dist/local-exec-daemon/main.cjs with serviceName `sand-local-exec-daemon`); it is not a detached ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE process, and a normal quit kills it (killLocalExecDaemon in the before-quit handler; only a restart-for-update leaves it running). Its parent is the main app process, so the probe folds it into the app row, and its bash -c command shells are its children, not the app's. A utility process has argv `Grok Bot Helper --type=utility --utility-sub-type=node.mojom.NodeService ...`; the module path travels over IPC, so this rule is expected NOT to match anything in 0.63.0. It is kept only as a harmless catch-all (it can only match a Grok Bot binary that carries `local-exec-daemon` in an argument, e.g. a 0.18-style detached daemon); the actual argv is unverified because the app is not installed here.

Bots on the Cursor-hosted persistent cloud computer (one Linux computer per user, shared by all their Bots), plus the iOS and Android apps. Every turn runs here. Nothing to see from this Mac; report the desktop app as a client with no turn state.

working_signals.meaning: The desktop app rewrites a per-account, per-Bot rolling chat replica (.blob, JSON, capped at about 200 entries) as chat entries arrive while the app is open. Raises working, never lowers it. Not mappable to a process (the file belongs to an account and Bot, not a session), so the probe, which needs a per_session path, cannot evaluate it; a host detector may watch the newest mtime among files matching the glob. Nothing is written locally when the app is closed even though Bots keep working.

Last resort, Electron floor. The app tree also runs the React UI, a noVNC webview of the cloud desktop and a coordinator utility process, so CPU is never the only reason and cannot prove idle. In 0.63.0 the local-exec daemon and its bash -c command shells are descendants of the main process, so a local command in flight does raise tree CPU. tool_children was REMOVED: the shells are children of the daemon utility process, never direct children of the matched app process, so the signal could not fire.

waiting_signals.meaning: Sidebar shows Needs attention for a question, approval or handoff, versus Working or typing status. In-app only; no local file or process carries it (undocumented if one does).
Per-Bot Notifications setting sends an OS notification when the Bot finishes or needs input; suppressed while the app is focused. Not machine readable by a detector.

Enterprise OpenTelemetry Export only, server side. Records the outcome of an approval (allowed, denied, held, timed_out) after the fact, with approval_mode ask_human or local_tool_permission; it is not a live pending state.

hooks.config: not documented for Grok Bot. The Grok Bot docs never describe user hooks, but docs.x.ai/grok-bot/teams-and-enterprises names "a hook" among the deciders Action Recording logs, Cursor's OpenTelemetry wire reference records a `pre-tool hook` (decision.source=hook, approval_mode=hook) on Grok Bot, and the app bundle carries team.hooks.read and team.hooks.manage permission ids (so hooks look team-managed). Hooks would run in the cloud computer, not on this Mac. Where they are configured is unknown.

telemetry.how: Enterprise plan only, team setting Team Settings > OpenTelemetry Export, sent by Cursor's backend (not the desktop app) to the customer's collector as OTLP/HTTP binary protobuf to <base>/v1/logs and /v1/metrics, tagged cursor.surface=grok_bot. Bot events (cursor.grok_bot.shell_command, tool_decision, routine_run, message_delivery and others) need Action Recording turned on. Prompt and response text is a further opt-in. Not available to individual or Teams plans, and no local OTel endpoint exists.

CASS reads the desktop's chat-only, lossy rolling replicas from ~/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot/sand-client-persistence (override CASS_GROK_BOT_DATA_ROOT). File name is lowercase unpadded base32 plus .blob; the decoded key is sand.client.slice.account.auth0%7Cuser_<26-char ULID>.transcript.replicas.<agent uuid>. Content is JSON {schemaVersion:1, value:{entries:[...]}}, entry kinds message (role, content) and send-message, observed cap 200 entries, IDs and timestampMs per entry. A replica belongs to an account and agent, not a session or workspace
sources.evidence: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_agent_detection/blob/main/src/connectors/grok_bot.rs (constants REPLICA_PREFIX, REPLICA_SEPARATOR; fn source_roots, replica_key, parse_replica); its test fixture is a sanitized 13-entry excerpt from CASS issue 447, so 'proves the reported structure, not native-app interoperability'

sources.claim: the same sand-client-persistence directory also holds per-account encrypted secrets blobs (Electron safeStorage, 0600), so not every file there is a replica and the directory is sensitive

the glob's 48-character prefix is the base32 of the FIRST 30 BYTES of the key, which is `sand.client.slice.account.auth` (NOT `...auth0`, as an earlier draft said); because the key is 65 bytes up to the replica separator (26 + 13 + a 26-character ULID) and 65 is a multiple of 5, the base32 of `.transcript.replicas` is a fixed 32-character block at characters 104-135, so the glob pins the replica suffix with 56 `?` between and excludes non-replica blobs such as the safeStorage secrets
sources.evidence: python3: base64.b32decode('onqw4zbomnwgszlooqxhg3djmnss4yldmnxxk3tufzqxk5di'.upper()) printed b'sand.client.slice.account.auth'; base64.b32encode(b'.transcript.replicas').decode().lower() printed fz2heyloonrxe2lqoqxhezlqnruwgylt (32 chars). fnmatch of the row glob against base32(KEY)+'.blob' for CASS's own test KEY `sand.client.slice.account.auth0%7Cuser_00000000000000000000000000.transcript.replicas.81da155f-cc4c-58b3-aadf-770858d5e55c` (201 chars) printed True, True for a second ULID-shaped key, and False for keys ending `.secrets` and `.transcript.send-journal.x`. Assumes the 26-character ULID subject that CASS grok_bot.rs (line 135) also requires; an account with another subject shape is not matched. Never open a match without decoding its name.

notes: Grok Bot is not a process-visible agent in the way a CLI is. The Bots run on a Cursor-hosted cloud computer and keep working with the app closed, so no local signal (process, child, CPU, file write) can say a turn is in progress: a turn with the app quit is invisible, and an open app with a working Bot is only sometimes visible through a chat-replica write. What a Mac can see is (1) the desktop client, (2) local command execution when the user has enabled Execution on Local Computer (only as tree CPU), and (3) a lossy chat replica. Report the desktop app as a client and treat working as best effort; the precise turn state exists only in Cursor's backend, the in-app sidebar, and Enterprise OTel. Confidence is documented, not verified-locally: the app is not installed here. The app surface (path, executable name, bundle id, helper names) was re-read from the vendor's own 0.63.0 zip and Info.plist, so it no longer rests on the 0.18.0 teardown. Still inferred: the argv of a running process (never seen live), the daemon's argv (expected to carry no `local-exec-daemon`, so that surface is inert), the replica file format (CASS source and a user-reported sample), and userData resolving to Application Support/Grok Bot. Matching reads argv only: the main app matches on argv[0] containing /Grok Bot.app/Contents/MacOS/Grok Bot, which no helper, no computer-use helper and no other row reaches. tool_children was dropped because the daemon (a utility process under main) owns the command shells, so they are never direct children of the matched app process. The replica files are keyed by account and Bot, never map a process to one; the glob is pinned to replica-shaped names but a detector must still decode the filename and require .transcript.replicas. before opening any file, because sand-client-persistence also holds encrypted secrets.
